For statistical computation, you can use a method such as ITERATIVE-R (Lu, Chen & Kou, 2003), or another appropriate method of your choosing, to determine this. Be aware that a naive single comparison against neighbors can suffer from a known bias called 'masking', where an extreme borough distorts the very baseline used to judge it -- your method should account for this.
 
Note: dedicated spatial-statistics packages (pysal, esda, libpysal, geopandas, or similar) are NOT installed in this environment -- implement this directly using only pandas and numpy.

Thought: Compute neighbor means, fit regression of GHG on neighbor mean for all boroughs, then compute externally studentized residual (t-stat) for City of London to test outlier status.  
Action:
```python
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np

# Load data
ghg = pd.read_csv('chunks_csv/outlierr/2021_ghg.csv')
adj = pd.read_csv('chunks_csv/borough_adjacency.csv')

# Compute neighbor means
# Merge adjacency borough -> neighbor GHG
adj_ghg = adj.merge(ghg, left_on='neighbor', right_on='borough', how='left', suffixes=('','_nbr'))
# Now group by original borough
nbr_means = adj_ghg.groupby('borough')['GHG_value_nbr'].mean().reset_index().rename(columns={'GHG_value_nbr':'M'})
# Merge back to get list of boroughs with neighbor means
df = ghg.merge(nbr_means, on='borough', how='left')
# Drop any boroughs with no neighbors (NaN M)
df = df.dropna(subset=['M']).reset_index(drop=True)

# Prepare regression X matrix: [1, M]
n = len(df)
X = np.vstack([np.ones(n), df['M'].values]).T
y = df['GHG_value'].values

# OLS estimates
XtX_inv = np.linalg.inv(X.T.dot(X))
beta = XtX_inv.dot(X.T).dot(y)
# Predictions and residuals
y_hat = X.dot(beta)
resid = y - y_hat

# Compute hat values (leverages)
H = X.dot(XtX_inv).dot(X.T)
h = np.diag(H)

# Overall MSE
p = X.shape[1]  # number of parameters (2)
df_resid = n - p
SSR = np.sum(resid**2)
MSE = SSR / df_resid

# Find index for City of London
city_idx = df.index[df['borough']=='City of London'][0]
e_i = resid[city_idx]
h_i = h[city_idx]

# Compute studentized residual (externally)
# s_(i)^2 = ((n-p)*MSE - e_i^2/(1-h_i)) / (n-p-1)
s_i_sq = ((df_resid)*MSE - e_i**2/(1-h_i)) / (df_resid - 1)
t_i = e_i / (np.sqrt(s_i_sq) * np.sqrt(1 - h_i))

print("City of London GHG:", df.loc[city_idx,'GHG_value'])
print("Neighbor mean M:", df.loc[city_idx,'M'])
print("Residual e_i:", e_i)
print("Leverage h_i:", h_i)
print("Externally studentized residual t_i:", t_i)
```

```python
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np

# Load data
ghg = pd.read_csv(DATASET_PATH)
adj = pd.read_csv(ADJACENCY_PATH)

# Compute neighbor means
# Merge adjacency (borough->neighbor) with ghg for neighbor values
adj_ghg = adj.merge(ghg, left_on='neighbor', right_on='borough', how='left')
# Now adj_ghg has columns: borough (orig), neighbor, GHG_value (neighbor)
nbr_means = adj_ghg.groupby('borough')['GHG_value'].mean().reset_index().rename(columns={'GHG_value':'M'})

# Merge back to ghg
df = ghg.merge(nbr_means, on='borough', how='left').dropna(subset=['M']).reset_index(drop=True)

# Regression of y on X = [1, M]
n = len(df)
X = np.vstack([np.ones(n), df['M'].values]).T
y = df['GHG_value'].values
# OLS
XtX_inv = np.linalg.inv(X.T.dot(X))
beta = XtX_inv.dot(X.T).dot(y)
y_hat = X.dot(beta)
resid = y - y_hat
# Leverage
H = X.dot(XtX_inv).dot(X.T)
h = np.diag(H)

# SSE
p = X.shape[1]
SSE = np.sum(resid**2)

# City of London index
i = df.index[df['borough']=='City of London'][0]
e_i = resid[i]
h_i = h[i]

# Leave-one-out SSE_i and MSE_i
SSE_i = SSE - e_i**2 / (1 - h_i)
MSE_i = SSE_i / (n - p - 1)

# Externally studentized residual
t_i = e_i / np.sqrt(MSE_i * (1 - h_i))

print("t_i:", t_i)
```

Thought: Fix merge by renaming adjacency columns to avoid duplicate 'borough'; then compute external studentized residual.  
Action:
```python
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np

# Load data
ghg = pd.read_csv(DATASET_PATH)
adj = pd.read_csv(ADJACENCY_PATH)

# Rename adjacency to avoid collision
adj = adj.rename(columns={'borough':'orig', 'neighbor':'nbr'})

# Merge to get neighbor GHG
adj_ghg = adj.merge(ghg.rename(columns={'borough':'nbr', 'GHG_value':'GHG_nbr'}),
                    on='nbr', how='left')

# Compute neighbor means per original borough
nbr_means = adj_ghg.groupby('orig')['GHG_nbr'].mean().reset_index().rename(columns={'orig':'borough', 'GHG_nbr':'M'})

# Merge neighbor means to ghg
df = ghg.merge(nbr_means, on='borough', how='left').dropna(subset=['M']).reset_index(drop=True)

# Regression y ~ 1 + M
n = len(df)
X = np.vstack([np.ones(n), df['M'].values]).T
y = df['GHG_value'].values
XtX_inv = np.linalg.inv(X.T.dot(X))
beta = XtX_inv.dot(X.T).dot(y)
y_hat = X.dot(beta)
resid = y - y_hat

# Leverage
H = X.dot(XtX_inv).dot(X.T)
h = np.diag(H)

# SSE
p = X.shape[1]  # parameters
SSE = np.sum(resid**2)

# Index of City of London
i = df.index[df['borough']=='City of London'][0]
e_i = resid[i]
h_i = h[i]

# Leave-one-out SSE_i
SSE_i = SSE - e_i**2 / (1 - h_i)
MSE_i = SSE_i / (n - p - 1)

# External studentized residual
t_i = e_i / np.sqrt(MSE_i * (1 - h_i))

print("City of London t_i:", t_i)
```
